approach: Add `pub fn check_request_coverage(reading, request, corrections, continued)` to reading.rs and call it from `check_reading_acceptance` right after `check_governance_coverage`. `check_reading_acceptance` gains a `corrections: &[String]` parameter (the current job's correction lines); the read path at line 520 passes them, taken from the `history` argument of that function, whose second element is the correction that followed each earlier reading (built at 994-1006). The replay call at 3012 passes `&[]`. Parts come from the request and from the retried or followed-up jobs' requests. A part is refused when no criterion covers it or an out_of_scope item defers it. A deferral stated by the request owner (the request, the current corrections, or each continued job's `EarlierAttempt.corrections`) exempts the part, last statement winning. Round-2 changes kept: five marker styles, one stem function, the SPECIFIC/GENERIC cover rule, 'part N' deferral forms. New in this round: (1) corrections are a request-side source with imperative deferral patterns; (2) in a request with an `Acceptance:` section, only line-start markers and the Acceptance bullets are parts, so quoted evidence in the middle of a line cannot become parts; (3) edited fixtures stay in the false-refusal list in their original form; (4) out_of_scope rule (c) needs two shared specific stems. Also: a sixth READING_RULES line, tests, and a CHANGELOG entry with measured counts.

decisions.choice: Put the check in reading.rs as `check_request_coverage(reading, request, corrections: &[String], continued: &[&EarlierAttempt])`, called from `check_reading_acceptance` after `check_governance_coverage`. Return Ok when capability is None, question is Some, or deliverables are empty. Compute `continued_jobs(request, attempt, referenced)` once (it is used at 2606 already) and reuse it. Parts come from `request`, the retried `attempt` always, and followed-up jobs only when they did not land. Each part remembers its source job.
decisions.reason: check_reading_acceptance (2599) is the one gate for the first read, the retry read (call at 520) and replay (3012). For a retry the request text ('try again on <id>') has no parts; they live in EarlierAttempt.request. `continued_jobs` already picks which earlier jobs a reading must account for.

rejected.option: Check only `request`
rejected.why: A retry request has no parts, so a retry could drop part (3) unchecked.

rejected.option: Take parts from every continued job whatever its end state
rejected.why: A landed job's parts are done; demanding criteria for them refuses correct readings.

rejected.option: Edit reader or verifier prompts
rejected.why: Prose only; the reader prompt has 3 tokens of headroom; the mechanism default needs a code check.

rejected.option: Check at verification
rejected.why: Too late: the producer has already run on a narrowed scope.

decisions.choice: Answer to finding 1 (corrections). Add a `corrections: &[String]` parameter to `check_reading_acceptance` (new 6th argument; existing test call sites get `&[]`, a mechanical edit that changes no fixture) and to `check_request_coverage`. The read path at reading.rs:520 passes `history.iter().filter_map(|(_, c)| c.clone())` collected into a Vec (history is the function's own parameter, line 379; its Option<String> is the correction or answer that followed each earlier reading, including the line just given, see 994-1006). The replay call at 3012 passes `&[]`. For each continued job, `EarlierAttempt.corrections` is also read (it already carries the corrections of the jobs it retried, 1124-1137). Owner sources are scanned oldest to newest: the retried jobs' corrections, the request, the current corrections. For each part and each source, sentences (split at newline, '. ' or '; ') that name the part are classified: DEFER if the sentence holds a request deferral pattern or a correction deferral pattern, with no negation before it and no reporting cue; REINSTATE if it holds a deferral pattern after a negation, or one of 'back in scope', 'in scope again', 'put it back', 'do it after all'; otherwise no change. The last DEFER or REINSTATE decides: DEFER exempts the part. A correction sentence names a part when it holds the label ('(3)', '3)', 'part 3', 'item 3'; letters likewise) or when `names_part` (decision 4 strict overlap) holds. Request patterns: 'is out of scope', 'are out of scope', 'is a follow-up', 'is a follow up', 'is for a follow-up', 'is for a later job', 'can wait', 'can be deferred', 'is deferred', 'is not part of this job', 'is not in this job', 'leave it for later'. Added for corrections (imperative): 'drop', 'skip', 'defer', 'leave out', 'leave it out', 'do it later', 'later job', 'later request', 'follow-up', 'follow up', 'out of scope', 'not now'. Bare 'follow-up' or 'deferred' in a request never exempts.
decisions.reason: Without it, a user who corrects a reading with 'drop (3), do it in a later job' gets a reader that complies and a gate that refuses it, so the job fails after one re-read. A correction is the request owner speaking; the brief keeps owner deferrals legal. Reporting-cue and negation rules keep 'the earlier reading said (3) is a follow-up; that was wrong' from exempting.

rejected.option: Append correction text to the request string at the call site
rejected.why: The parts parser would read corrections as parts, and `followed_up_ids(request)` would pick up job ids cited in corrections and change `continued_jobs`.

rejected.option: Ignore corrections
rejected.why: Refuses readings the user asked for (finding 1).

rejected.option: Any correction line naming the label exempts
rejected.why: 'do not defer (3)' or 'the reading wrongly dropped (3)' would switch the check off.

rejected.option: A separate check_reading_acceptance_with wrapper keeping the 5-argument form
rejected.why: Then check_reading_acceptance would not call check_request_coverage itself, and criterion 5 and the single-gate story weaken; the call-site edit is mechanical.

decisions.choice: Parts parser: styles `(N)`, `N)`, `N.`, `(a)`, `a)`. A leading '- ' or '* ' is skipped before the line-start test. `N)`, `N.`, `a)` count only at line start (`N.` needs '. ' after the digits, so '3.5' is no marker). `(N)` and `(a)` count at line start, and, only when the request has no `Acceptance:` heading, also after ':' ';' '.' ',' plus whitespace, and must not be followed directly by ',' or ')'. A part's text runs to the next marker of the same run or the end of its line. Per style take the longest sequential run from 1 (or a); a run is a parts list only if at least two markers hold a stem. Answer to finding 2: when the request has an `Acceptance:` line (case-insensitive), only line-start markers and the Acceptance bullets (the bullets after that line up to the first blank or non-bullet line) are parts; mid-line markers are ignored. Acceptance bullets are labelled by their text. Both come from the shared `request_bullets` helper that `request_text_acceptance` also uses.
decisions.reason: '1. x 2. y 3. z' is the commonest way to write explicit parts. Steward bodies quote free text on one line (hestia.rs:343-345 writes 'prevention it proposed: {prevention}' through `one_line`), so a prevention '(1) add X; (2) add Y' sits mid-line and, with an Acceptance section present, is not a part. Line-start markers cannot come from the Steward body: `StewardRequest` refuses body lines that start like a bullet, and quoted text is collapsed to one line. Requests with an Acceptance section and real numbered lines (a human request) keep those parts.

rejected.option: With an Acceptance section take only its bullets as parts
rejected.why: Drops a human request's own numbered lines whenever it also lists Acceptance bullets.

rejected.option: Skip lines starting 'Introspection '
rejected.why: Ties the parser to one renderer; spec and throughput renderers quote text too.

rejected.option: Only `(N)` plus Acceptance bullets
rejected.why: Leaves '1. x 2. y 3. z' requests unchecked.

rejected.option: Treat every bullet or numbered line as a part
rejected.why: Wider than the failure class; plain lists cause false refusals.

rejected.option: A model call to compare parts and criteria
rejected.why: Costs a call and is not deterministic; the other reading checks cost none.

decisions.choice: One `stems(text) -> BTreeSet<String>`: `stem_word` lowercases, splits on non-letters, strips one suffix (ing, ed, es, s; not 's' after 's') if 3+ letters remain, then one trailing 'e'. Stems of 3 letters or fewer are dropped (so name/names/named and fix/fixed are never compared). STOP is `stem_word` of the raw function words (with, that, this, which, should, would, from, when, each, only, same, without, before, after, into, also, about, them, then, there, where, other, have, been, were, does, must, will, than, such, more, most, some, both, they, what, your, these, those, while, because, still, request, reading, part, parts, item, items, job). GENERIC is `stem_word` of: test, check, pass, fail, change, cargo, file, code. `covers(part, text)`: n part stems, s of them outside GENERIC. n = 0: skipped. s >= 2: at least one shared specific stem, and when n >= 4 at least 2 shared in all. s = 1: if n <= 3 the shared stems must include that specific stem; if n >= 4 at least 3 shared in all. s = 0: at least min(2, n) shared. A criterion also covers part N when it names '(N)', 'part N' or 'part (N)' (letters likewise).
decisions.reason: Stop list and text pass through the same function, so they cannot disagree. Hand traces: Steward bullet A 'A test fails without the change and passes with it, for the cause and not only for one job' = {test,fail,chang,pass,caus}, n=5, s=1, needs 3 shared; 'A new test fails on the code before the change and passes after it' shares test, fail, chang, pass, so it covers; bare 'cargo test passes' does not. Bullet B 'The root cause is named in the change description and fixed where it originates, not at one instance' = {root,caus,chang,description,originat,instanc}, n=6, s=5; 'CHANGELOG.md has an entry that names the root cause and the new check' shares root and caus and covers it. Bullet C 'fmt, clippy and test pass' = {clippy,test,pass}, n=3, s=1; needs clippy; 'cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked: all pass' covers it.

rejected.option: Any 2 shared stems for parts of 4 or more stems
rejected.why: Generic test/pass/check would cover almost any part.

rejected.option: A hand-written stop list of test, pass, fail, change
rejected.why: Strips bullet A to {caus}, which no ordinary criterion shares.

rejected.option: Keep 3-letter stems that came from longer words
rejected.why: Adds tokens like 'nam' that match unrelated words.

decisions.choice: Deferral by out_of_scope. An item defers part N when (a) it names 'part N', 'part (N)', 'item N' or 'item (N)' (whole word, case-insensitive; letters likewise), or (b) it names the bare label and holds a deferral phrase, or (c) `names_part(part, item)` holds and it holds a deferral phrase. Answer to finding 4: `names_part` is stricter than `covers`: the part must have s >= 2 specific stems and the item must share at least 2 of them (if s < 2, rule (c) does not apply and only (a) and (b) can defer it). Deferral phrases: follow-up, follow up, later job, later request, separate request, separate job, next job, another job, defer. A bare '(3)' or 'finding (3)' with no deferral phrase is not a deferral. A deferral refuses even when a criterion covers the part. Tests: 'the display polish is a follow-up' against part '(3) add the status timeout display' (one shared specific stem, 'display') is accepted; 'the status timeout display is a follow-up' is refused.
decisions.reason: Retry readings often number an earlier job's findings in out_of_scope; 'finding (3) of job X is not touched' must not read as dropping request part (3). One shared specific stem is too weak to say an item is about the part, so a narrowing item about a related detail would be read as a deferral. Overlap needs a deferral phrase so ordinary exclusions stay legal.

rejected.option: Any out_of_scope item that names the label is a deferral
rejected.why: Refuses retries that number earlier findings.

rejected.option: Reuse `covers` for rule (c)
rejected.why: One shared specific stem triggers it (finding 4).

rejected.option: Refuse any out_of_scope item that shares words with a part
rejected.why: Refuses legitimate narrowing.

decisions.choice: Complaint cues and negation, shared by decisions 2 and 5. A sentence is a complaint when it holds, as a whole word or phrase: said, says, claimed, claims, wrong, wrongly, mistaken, rejected, earlier, previous, 'the reading', 'was refused'. A negation token (not, no, never, cannot, don't, any n't word, without) before a deferral pattern turns it into a REINSTATE, not a DEFER. A complaint sentence changes nothing.
decisions.reason: 'The earlier reading said (3) is a follow-up; that was wrong' must keep part (3) in scope. A false refusal costs one re-read; a false exemption ships the failure.

rejected.option: Exempt on any deferral phrase near the part
rejected.why: Negated and complaining mentions would switch the check off.

rejected.option: No owner exemption
rejected.why: The brief says a request that itself defers a part still accepts a reading deferring it.

decisions.choice: The refusal error names each problem by part label and text, the reason (no covering criterion, or deferred by the quoted out_of_scope item) and the repair: add a criterion, remove the out_of_scope item, or have the request or a correction defer the part. A part from an earlier job also names that job. Deliverables are not text-compared.
decisions.reason: The reader gets one re-read with the refusal text. A Deliverable holds only a path, so mapping it to part text is guesswork.

rejected.option: Also require a deliverable per part
rejected.why: Paths cannot be compared with part text reliably.

Measure the section length once with a temporary eprintln under --nocapture, remove it, state the byte count in the CHANGELOG. Shorten the line, never raise the 2400 cap.

decisions.choice: False-refusal count (answers finding 3). A test `false_refusals_over_existing_fixtures` runs `check_request_coverage` over a const FIXTURES list of (name, request, original criteria/out_of_scope) entries: the request literals with parts or Acceptance bullets from existing reading tests (producer greps the tests at 5901-6893), each with that test's reading as it was before the change, plus Steward requests (`root_cause_request` output if callable from athena-core tests, else text built with the same format strings from hestia.rs 323-352, and the bullets at hestia.rs:348-351, steward.rs ~534 and ~674; the test comment says which) paired with ordinary criteria. Any existing test whose fixture must be edited so the new gate accepts it keeps its ORIGINAL pair in FIXTURES, so the refusal counts; the test asserts refused == EXPECTED_FALSE_REFUSALS (0 unless explained) and EDITED_TESTS lists each edited test by name. The CHANGELOG shows 'false refusals: {refused} of {total}' from those constants and names each edited test next to the count. The call-site edit that adds `&[]` is a signature change and does not count as an edit of a fixture.

risks.risk: Stem-overlap coverage is heuristic: it may wrongly refuse a reworded reading or accept one that shares common words.
risks.mitigation: Specific stems need a specific match; generic stems count fully only when the part has at most one specific stem; a criterion naming '(N)' or 'part N' also covers. Steward bullets are hand-traced and tested; the error states the repair; the reader gets one re-read. Known leniency: a part with one specific stem and four generic ones is covered by any criterion sharing three stems.

risks.risk: Reading parts from earlier jobs' requests refuses retries that legitimately narrow, or follow-ups of landed work.
risks.mitigation: Parts come from the retried attempt, plus followed-up jobs only when they did not land. Any criterion of the new reading can cover a part. Owner corrections of those jobs can exempt a part. The retry test and the fixture count show it.

risks.risk: Correction handling misses a phrasing ('hold off on (3)') and the gate refuses a reading the user asked for.
risks.mitigation: The pattern lists are fixed and tested; the error tells the reader to cite the correction in a criterion or out-of-scope-free restatement, and a false refusal costs one re-read. The first DEFER/REINSTATE-last-wins rule is tested both ways. Replay at verification shows false refusals. Open question below.

risks.risk: A correction that merely mentions a part ('(3) looks fine') is read wrongly.
risks.mitigation: Only sentences with a deferral pattern, no negation and no complaint cue change state; others change nothing.

risks.risk: With an Acceptance heading present, inline `(N)` parts in a human request are no longer enforced.
risks.mitigation: Line-start markers and bullets still count; the Acceptance bullets normally restate parts. Stated in the doc comment and a test.

risks.risk: Parsing `N.` and `N)` lines adds parts from ordinary numbered steps.
risks.mitigation: Runs must start at 1 with two or more markers that hold a stem; '3.5' and mid-line '1.' are not markers; coverage is lenient; the fixture count measures common cases.

risks.risk: The real newly refused share may exceed 5%.
risks.mitigation: 5% is labelled an estimate; replay at verification measures the real share (it passes no earlier attempts or corrections, so it cannot see the retry or correction paths); the check is tuned lenient.

risks.risk: Adding the `corrections` argument touches many test call sites (about 40) and could be mistaken for fixture edits.
risks.mitigation: The edit is `, &[]` only; the helper at 5594 centralises most; any real fixture change goes in the edited list and keeps its original pair in FIXTURES.

risks.risk: Refactoring request_text_acceptance onto request_bullets changes `athena plan`'s parse.
risks.mitigation: `request_bullets` returns exactly the lines returned before (same trim, same is_bullet); the existing Steward tests (hestia.rs ~2306, ~2833) run in cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: A stray 'pub fn check_request_coverage' string earlier in reading.rs breaks the source-text split in the doc test.
risks.mitigation: Define it once before the tests module; write the intended-refusal paragraph last in its doc.

risks.mitigation: Keep the line to 190 bytes or less; run cargo test -p athena-context; shorten the line, never raise a cap.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in the reading.rs tests module call the production gate `check_reading_acceptance(&reading, request, attempt, &[], None, corrections)` (the existing 5-argument signature at 2599 plus the new `corrections` parameter added by step 5). Preconditions: capability Some, question None, deliverables non-empty, Content-kind criteria so check_code_survey does not trigger. Fixture: the existing `scoped_reading` helper (4992) with `acceptance_criteria` replaced by criteria covering parts (1) and (2) only and out_of_scope 'Part (3) is deferred to a follow-up request'. (a) First attempt: request is the '(1) ... (2) ... (3) ...' text of job 20261029-084645-sza7; the test comment says plainly that the text is rebuilt from the brief because records/ is absent. (b) Retry: request 'try again on 20261012-084936-n1p0' (PRIOR_JOB), `attempt` is `Some(&EarlierAttempt { request: <that parts text>, ..prior() })` (`prior()` exists at 5047), summary starts 'Retry <PRIOR_JOB>:' with non-empty deliverables and out_of_scope so check_prior_result_and_scope passes. Both seams exist today; no double. Controls: same readings with the out_of_scope item removed and a criterion for (3) added return Ok(()).
demonstrations.observes: Cases (a) and (b) return Err whose message contains '(3)' and the quoted out_of_scope item; (b) also names the earlier job. The controls return Ok(()).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without check_request_coverage (or without the continued-jobs argument for the retry case) check_reading_acceptance returns Ok for these readings, so the unwrap_err assertions fail on the code before the change.

demonstrations.method: Tests through `check_reading_acceptance` with `scoped_reading` (exists) and replaced criteria. Request shapes with no Acceptance heading: '(1) add X ... (2) add Y ... (3) add Z' inline and on lines; '1. ...' lines; '1) ...' lines; '(a) ... (b) ... (c) ...'; 'a) ...' lines. For each shape three readings: criteria for items 1-2 only; criteria for 1-2 plus out_of_scope 'Item 3 is a follow-up'; criteria for every item. Extra cases: (i) mixed part '(3) add a status test that checks the timeout passes' with criteria for (1) and (2) plus the single criterion 'cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test --locked: all pass' (refused); (ii) the same with a criterion 'the status test checks that the timeout passes' (accepted); (iii) reworded: part 'The root cause is named in the change description', criterion 'CHANGELOG.md names the root cause' (accepted); (iv) this job's own request text, whose quoted 'such as (1), (2) and (3). It requires' yields no parts (accepted); (v) out_of_scope 'finding (3) of job X is not touched' with part (3) covered (accepted); (vi) out_of_scope 'Part (3) is not touched' with no deferral phrase, refused by the 'part N' form; (vii) out_of_scope 'the display polish is a follow-up' against part '(3) add the status timeout display' (accepted) and 'the status timeout display is a follow-up' (refused).
demonstrations.observes: The first two readings of every shape, and cases (i), (vi) and the refused half of (vii), return Err naming item 3. The covering readings and cases (ii), (iii), (iv), (v) and the accepted half of (vii) return Ok(()).
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check each refused case is accepted and its is_err assertion fails. A parser that handled only `(N)` leaves the '1.', '1)' and lettered cases Ok. Without the SPECIFIC/GENERIC rule case (i) is accepted. With a too-strict match the covering cases are refused. With the one-stem rule (c) the narrowing item in (vii) is refused.

demonstrations.method:
Tests through `check_reading_acceptance` with `scoped_reading`. (a) Request 'Fix X

Acceptance:
- A test fails without the change and passes with it, for the cause and not only for one job

demonstrations.method: Tests through `check_reading_acceptance` with `scoped_reading`. Request: '(1) add X; (2) add Y; (3) add Z. The earlier reading said (3) is a follow-up; that was wrong.' Reading has criteria for (1) and (2) and out_of_scope 'Part (3) is a follow-up'. Variants: 'the reading deferred part (3) to a follow-up'; 'an earlier attempt claimed (3) is out of scope'. Control: '(3) add Z; (3) is a follow-up' without a cue is accepted. The same complaint passed as a correction string ('the earlier reading wrongly dropped (3)') also refuses.
demonstrations.observes: The complaint variants return Err naming (3); the control returns Ok(()).
demonstrations.fails_without: If reported mentions exempted, the reading deferring (3) would be accepted and the Err assertion fails. Without the cue test 'the earlier reading said (3) is a follow-up; that was wrong' exempts part (3).

demonstrations.method: Source-text test in the reading.rs tests module in the style of `prior_result_refusal_is_declared_intended` (5530): `include_str!("reading.rs")`, split at `pub fn check_request_coverage`, take the doc paragraphs before it, assert they hold the root-cause sentence (the gate 'does not compare' the request's named parts with the reading) and both job ids 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k. Assert the text of `check_reading_acceptance` up to the next `pub fn` contains `check_request_coverage(reading, request,`. The literal `pub fn check_request_coverage` appears once, outside test code. The verifier can also Grep reading.rs for `check_request_coverage` and the two ids.
demonstrations.observes: The doc comment holds both ids and the root-cause sentence, and the call is inside check_reading_acceptance.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the function, its doc or the call were missing, the include_str test fails (nothing to split on, or the call string absent).

demonstrations.method: Whole-crate run on the real gate. (i) A declaration test as at line 5530: `replay_declaration` on a criterion containing 'expected 5% of newly refused readings' gives share Some(5); the check's last doc paragraph holds 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.', says 5% is an estimate and that replay passes no earlier attempts or corrections. (ii) `false_refusals_over_existing_fixtures` (decision 9) runs the check over FIXTURES built from the existing reading-test requests (original readings, including those of any edited test) and the Steward requests, and asserts refused == EXPECTED_FALSE_REFUSALS and the edited-test list equals EDITED_TESTS. (iii) All existing reading, replay and acceptance tests run; one that fails because its request has parts is counted in (ii) and its fixture criteria are fixed, not the check. Only the added `&[]` argument changes at existing call sites. The test does not measure the 5%; the replay at verification measures that from records/, which the snapshot lacks.
demonstrations.observes: Declared share parses as 5; the doc sentence is present; the false-refusal count equals the stated constant and edited tests are listed; every existing test passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the declaration were missing the declaration test fails. If the check were absent the criterion 1 tests in the same run fail. If the check wrongly refused an existing fixture, that existing test or the count test fails.

demonstrations.method: Existing test `the_reader_brief_names_each_reading_rule_in_one_short_line` (briefs.rs ~3172) through the real `reader_brief`. Seam exists today; step 8 changes READING_RULES to six lines and adds `check_request_coverage` to the checks array. The test asserts one line per rule, each at most 220 bytes, each check named, and the section under 2400 bytes. The producer reads the section length once (temporary eprintln under --nocapture, then removed) and writes it in the CHANGELOG.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes with 6 rule lines and the section under 2400 bytes; the CHANGELOG states the measured byte count.
demonstrations.fails_without: If READING_RULES gains a sixth line but its array size or the checks list is not updated, the test fails with a count or 'no rule for check_request_coverage' error. If the section passes 2400 bytes the size assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: Run the three gates over the workspace on the real tree. No double or seam.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.fails_without: Unused helpers fail clippy (dead_code under -D warnings); bad formatting fails fmt; a check that refuses a fixture reading, a missed `&[]` call site, or a briefs.rs array mismatch fails build or cargo test.

demonstrations.method: A changelog test beside the criterion 6 declaration test: normalise white space in include_str!("../../../CHANGELOG.md") and assert it holds 'check_request_coverage', 'root cause', '20261029-084645-sza7', '20261029-110953-bw7k', 'refuses more readings', 'expected 5% of newly refused readings', and the string 'false refusals: {refused} of {total}' built from the false-refusal test's constants. The entry is under [Unreleased] > Added. A Grep of CHANGELOG.md for check_request_coverage shows the same.
demonstrations.observes: The entry names the root cause, the check, the measured false-refusal count with edited tests, and the rule-section byte count.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the CHANGELOG entry the include_str assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Correction tests (answer to finding 1), through `check_reading_acceptance` with `scoped_reading`, request '(1) add X; (2) add Y; (3) add Z', criteria for (1) and (2), out_of_scope 'Part (3) is deferred to a follow-up'. (a) corrections `&[]`: refused naming (3). (b) corrections `&["drop (3), do it in a later job".to_string()]`: accepted. (c) correction '(3) is a follow-up' accepted; 'do not defer (3)' refused; '(3) is a follow-up' then a later 'put (3) back in scope' refused (last wins). (d) retry: `attempt` is `Some(&EarlierAttempt { corrections: vec!["(3) is a follow-up"], ..prior() })` carrying request with the parts: accepted; without that correction refused. This is a second block for criterion 4's behavior (complaint and owner statements are told apart), run in the same command.
demonstrations.observes: (a) Err naming (3); (b), (c) first form and (d) with correction Ok(()); the other forms Err.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without correction handling (b) and (d) are refused and fail their Ok assertions; with a request-only exemption they stay refused.
